When using this setting, your Pro 34 isn't going to constantly create clouds of dark, thick smoke, which is what pellet grills are intentionally designed not to do. Instead, these grills, regardless of manufacturer, will create what is called ‘blue smoke’, as it is the highly preferred type used for cooking. The Smoke setting will basically keep the grill running at its lowest temperature range, which not only keeps the food exposed longer, but also causes the greatest production of blue smoke as well. As for the temperature dropping, while this is usually related to simple causes, such not having enough clearance between food/trays and the interior walls for proper airflow, ash building up in the firepot, opening the lid frequently, or compromised pellets, it can even be due to the way the startup is performed (keep lid closed until temperature is reached). ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thank you for reviewing the Pro 34. While proper grill maintenance is definitely a big help for ensuring the best performance, you might also want to include the bottom of the hopper as part of the cleaning process. Based on your description, with both the error code at low temperatures, as well as the jammed auger, it sounds like you may have a buildup of dust in the auger tube opening. Not only does this dust affect the grill's temperature by reducing the number of pellets getting to the firepot, but it can even lock up the auger when the fine particles absorb moisture from the air, then dry out in a solid clump. An easy way to avoid this is by scooping the pellets out of the bag as opposed to pouring the entire contents into the hopper. Although pellets will leave the mill with minimal dust, a substantial amount can sometimes develop during transportation and handling, then settle in the bottom of the bag. And while keeping the hopper clean of dust is much easier than clearing a auger jam, luckily it isn’t necessary to take the grill apart if a jam does occur. In fact, the only thing you’ll need to remove is the hopper box, which is held on by a few screws. Once it is out of the way, you’ll have full access to the auger and can deal with the jam. But if you have any questions during this process, or would just like some help doing it, Traeger Customer Service is always available to help. Give us a call up to 10:00 PM MT, any day of the year, and one of our agents will be happy to assist.

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thank you for reviewing the Pro 34. Although referring to the grill blowing up could be one way to describe a grease fire, it appears your only contact with Customer Service is actually for smoke coming out of the hopper. While this may seem alarming at first, it is really not a serious issue, and is simply the result of smoke back feeding through the auger tube, either due to the grill being on unlevel ground, a chimney cape that is set too low (should have a ¾” gap), a fan that isn’t spinning (try turning it with a stick to get it unstuck), or as you’ve already made sure is not the case, an excessive buildup of dust/ash in the firepot. In regard to the temperature variance, often times this is believed to be the case when using a third party device, such an oven thermometer or meat probe, to test the grills internal temperature. However, your Pro 34 does not measure heat the same way as either of these, but rather uses the 7” RTD probe in conjunction with the algorithms of the controller to take multiple factors into consideration, such as position, radiant heat and air flow, to provide a proper representation of the grill’s true internal temperature. For a more accurate test, try turning on a cold grill, and note the initial reading and compare it to the ambient air. Even though they are not technically made to measure external air temperature, if it is within 20 degrees, the probe should be working fine.

It is extremely rare for an auger to itself to actually break, as they are really just a heavy corkscrew shaped metal rod that pushes pellets to the fire. ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thank you for your review of the Pro 34. Most of the time when the grill has a problem reaching the set temperature, replacing the RTD won't make a difference. This part is simply measuring how hot the inside of the grill is and sending that information to the controller. You can do a simple test of the RTD when you first turn on the grill by comparing the initial reading to the ambient temperature at the time. If it is within 20 degrees above or below the outside air, then it is likely working ok. Aside from the RTD, there are several other things that can be checked if the grill is consistently running cool. Although you've probably used more than one bag already, pellets are still worth mentioning since they are responsible for the vast majority of issues like this. They should have a sheen to their exterior and take a little effort to break in half, snapping cleanly in two without crumbling. Also make sure that they are not being blocked by dust in the bottom of the hopper, as this can cause low temps as well. For other possibilities, search “running cool” on the Traeger website. You’ll find an article with everything mentioned here and a lot more. Or better yet, call Customer Service and have an agent go over your grill with you. No matter how old your Traeger is, you’ll always have access to our support line, 365 days a year.

ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thanks for your review of the Pro 34. What you are experiencing is really only attributable to a few things, so a resolution shouldn’t be that difficult. More often than not, this behavior is simply related to an issue with airflow. Without enough oxygen getting to the firepot, the pellets will smolder instead of burn, creating the exact type of smoke you are seeing. Additionally, the pellets overflowing in the firepot is also indicative of the same problem, since the auger will feed pellets into a pot that is not going through them fast enough, and eventually they’ll all smolder to ash as seen in your photo. But whatever the cause, most of the time, the resolution will not be that complicated. And although troubleshooting with an agent may sound a little involved, it is very seldom the case. Often times the resolution is achieved with one short call and is typically not related to a malfunctioning part of the grill. But even in cases where something needs to be replaced, the process is almost always very simple, and the part will be sent at no cost to you as long as the grill is under warranty. While having us reimburse money or replace the entire grill may be preferred, please give us a chance to help you get your Traeger running. You might be surprised how easy it turns out to be, and it almost certainly won’t take hours on the line to do.

It’s not really that this model, or any Traeger for that matter, has a known problem with flameouts, but rather that it is something that can happen with any smoker, somewhat like an auger jam is possible with any pellet grill. Although rare, flameouts are typically the result of only a few different things, and luckily, all of them are avoidable. When working with Traeger support, the reason they focused on the flameout is because once the cause is determined and corrected, the subsequent fire will no longer be an issue. However, the most important thing to know is that if a pellet grill, regardless of brand, either doesn’t start properly or turns off without going through the shutdown process, you’ll always want to check the firepot once the grill has cooled completely and clear out any remaining pellets before turning it on again. Or even better than that, this would be the perfect time to reach out to Traeger support again.
